unit: Unit 12: Everyday Life with Your Computer
title: Writing a Document Online
drDigitalIntro:
Google Docs is a free word processor that runs in your web browser — no software to install.

Try it now on your own computer:

1. Open your web browser.
2. Go to docs.google.com (you'll need to sign in with a Google account — if you don't have one, you can create one for free).
3. Click the + Blank button to create a new document.
4. Type a short paragraph about anything you like — your favorite meal, a memory, what you did today.
5. Watch the top of the page: it says "Saving..." then "All changes saved." Your work is saved automatically — no need to click Save!

That's it — you just created a document that lives in the cloud and can be opened from any device.

playgroundTask.goal: You created a real document online and brought back its address

steps.say: Open a new tab and go to docs.google.com — sign in if it asks.
steps.detail: You need a Google account for this one. If you do not have one and do not want one today, that is fine — use Skip and come back later. Nothing after this lesson depends on it.

steps.say: Click the + Blank page to start a new document, and type one sentence.
steps.detail: Anything — 'This is my first online document' is perfect. Notice you never press Save; it saves as you type.

steps.say: Copy the document's address and paste it below.
steps.detail: Click once in the address bar at the top — the whole address highlights. Ctrl+C to copy, come back here, Ctrl+V in the box. That address IS your document — anyone you share it with later uses it.

drDigitalSuccess: You just made a document that lives on the internet — you can open it from any computer in the world by signing in. The next lesson shows you how to share it.
drDigitalHint: The address bar is the long box at the very top of the browser. One click selects the whole address; Ctrl+C copies it.
